description: ECMA-262 returns from `Number.prototype.toPrecision` at `If precision is undefined`, and at nothing else, so the entry is conditioned on the position getting nothing and the call site decides. The narrow form is what keeps that entry honest: `=nullish` here would bless `(1).toPrecision(null)`, which throws a RangeError, and would be true only because the declared type happens to exclude `null` — a fact the discharge deliberately never reads.

diagnostics.message: Call to `value.toPrecision` escapes this `@nothrow` function: the carrier that colors it declares it non-throwing given nothing is passed for `precision`, and this call passes something. Your outs: bridge this call with `try`/`catch`; or, if it cannot throw, report it against the shipped standard-library baseline at https://github.com/no-throw/no-throw/issues — the other three carriers are keyed by npm package name, and no key in that grammar reaches a `lib.*.d.ts` member.
